agents.role: Samples design variants inside the declared ranges, posts them as jobs, and keeps the winners: the feasible designs with the lowest thermal resistance.
Runs the heatsink simulator on every claimed job and on every held-out re-score. It computes scores from physics in code and never judges a design by any other means.
Records every failed variant with its score and its named violation, so the failure ledger is complete and checkable.
Keeps the proven record: which designs cleared the held-out gate, their scores, and their export files. It never marks a design proven that the gate did not pass.
The pack's only cross-world messenger. It sends proven-design summaries (id, artefact class, score, export path) to the crew and nothing else.

alerts.carries: The proven design id, its artefact class, its score, and its export file path.
The failed variant id, its score, and its named constraint violation.
The design id and which held-out check failed: claimed-score mismatch, bar miss, or held-out infeasibility.

receives.carries: Artefact class and design constraints for a requested run.

sends.carries: Proven design id, artefact class, score, and export file path.

parts.proven: Pinning tests in tests/officina/test_heatsink.py (golden resistance value, efficiency bounds, constraint boundaries, determinism). UNPROVEN, stated plainly: never validated against a measured physical heatsink.
parts.what: The heatsink fin simulator: straight rectangular aluminium fins on a flat base, scored by thermal resistance from fin-efficiency physics in code. No model calls, no network, no bus posts.

parts.proven: Pinning tests in tests/officina/test_design_loop.py (seeded replay, failure recording, winner order, held-out gate accept and reject paths, export file). UNPROVEN, stated plainly: never run on a booted Meta OS image or wired as a scheduled service.
parts.what: The design-job loop: post, claim, score, complete or fail with a reason; winners kept by score; held-out acceptance gate; overnight-style run recording and best-proven-design export. Pure core plus CLI, no model calls, no bus posts.

summary: The invention workshop: an agent that designs, simulates, breaks, and redesigns — thousands of iterations a night. Stage 1 runs one real artefact class (heatsink fin geometry) through a real simulator, a design-job loop, and a held-out acceptance gate. PARTIAL: the design loop, heatsink simulator, and held-out gate exist and are tested; every other declared watcher remains definition only, and nothing here runs a real manufacturing line.
summary_note: Design aid only: it proposes, scores, and records designs. It never orders a build, never ships a part, and never presents a simulated score as a measured result. A design counts as workshop-proven only after the held-out re-score passes, and even then a human decides whether anything gets built.

urgency.meaning: A design failure that would endanger a user if the part were built as drawn. Preempts everything else on the bus.
A held-out gate failure on a design already exported as proven. Act before the export is used.
Design proven, design failed, and run-completion notes.
Sealed overnight run records and score curves.

watchers.watches: Design jobs: which variants are posted, claimed, scored, kept as winners, or failed, in job order.
Simulator runs: the physics score of every variant and every held-out re-score, with the conditions each score was computed under.
Failures: every variant that broke a rule, with its score and its named violation, so a failed design is never silently dropped.
Workshop-proven designs: which designs cleared the held-out gate, their scores, and the files they were exported to.
